name: Anakonda

seo.title: Anakonda Cruise, Napo River, Ecuador | James Wild & Co
seo.description: Anakonda: a 16-suite, 36-guest river expedition vessel on Ecuador's Napo River from Coca. Three, four or seven nights near Yasuni.

tagline: Sixteen suites on the Napo, a half-hour flight from Quito.
answer: Anakonda is a 47 m river expedition vessel on the Napo River in the Ecuadorian Amazon, built in 2013. She takes up to 36 guests in 16 suites, four with private balconies, and runs three, four or seven nights from Coca, a 30-minute flight from Quito, near Yasuní National Park.
facts: Coca (embark via motorized canoe to Puerto Providencia)
overview: Anakonda was built in 2013 for Ecuador's Napo River. She is 47 m long with 16 suites: four 24 sq m Deluxe Suites with private balconies and whirlpool tubs on the third deck, and twelve 20 sq m Standard Suites with French balconies on the second, four of which connect.
Guests fly Quito to Coca, then ride a motorized canoe about 90 minutes downriver to board. The lounge, bar and spa are on the third deck; two motorized canoes run the excursions.
why: The operator calls her and her sister Manatee the only cruises on Ecuador's Amazon. The Napo gives Yasuní National Park, parrot clay licks and a canopy tower within a week, closer to Quito than any Peruvian boat is to Lima.

faqs: The Napo River in the Ecuadorian Amazon, from Coca, near Yasuní National Park.
Fly Quito to Coca (about 30 minutes), then a motorized canoe of about 90 minutes to the boat.
Three nights Sunday to Wednesday, four nights Wednesday to Sunday, or seven nights.
From US$2,995 per person for three nights, US$3,743 for four and US$5,990 for seven, in 2026.
Up to 36 in 16 suites, with 25 crew.
The four Deluxe Suites have private balconies and whirlpool tubs; the twelve Standard Suites have French balconies.

suits.line: Coca is a short flight from Quito, so it pairs with an island trip.
